findings.label: Comparative Law, Governance and Advocacy
findings.reason: A feasible programme builds comparative legal analysis, business law, public policy and advocacy. Its property, contract and criminal law coverage remains concentrated in broad comparative or thematic courses. Public speaking, negotiation and empirical methods complement the legal work but do not supply litigation procedure, pleading or supervised legal scholarship.

findings.label: Law, Technology and Environmental Governance
findings.reason: A feasible programme joins comparative and public law with climate governance. International environmental treaties, EU green and digital-market regulation and corporate AI regulation provide genuine legal or regulatory content. These topics are embedded in broader courses and do not build into a legal specialization with sustained analysis of legislation, cases and remedies.

alignment: Substantive partial relations include EU institutions and remedies, international treaties, property and contract, criminal responsibility, constitutional review and administrative fairness. No public UCR option or comparison alignment is selected.
